stem: Which of the following aerodigestive tract foreign bodies warrants the most urgent intervention?

options.text: A button battery lodged in the oesophagus
A smooth coin in the stomach in a well child
A small peanut aspiration with no respiratory symptoms
A non-obstructing oesophageal food bolus in a child who can swallow secretions
A blunt foreign body already in the colon

explanation: A button battery lodged in the oesophagus is a medical emergency because it can cause rapid liquefaction necrosis, perforation, and fistula formation. It requires urgent removal. The other scenarios may require observation or non-urgent management depending on symptoms and location.
rationale: The original question is a multiple-answer item, so it is rewritten into a single-best-answer question using the highest-risk scenario: a button battery in the oesophagus.

optionExplanations.A: Correct — oesophageal button batteries require urgent removal due to rapid caustic injury and risk of perforation/fistula.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect — a coin in the stomach of a stable child is usually observed if asymptomatic.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect — an asymptomatic small airway aspiration is concerning but the urgency depends on symptoms and obstruction; this is less immediately critical than an oesophageal button battery.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect — if the child can manage secretions and is not obstructed, this is not necessarily the most urgent scenario.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect — a foreign body already in the colon is generally not an urgent aerodigestive emergency.
